chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and another, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd Shabāb al-Ṣayrafī, from Mālik ibn Ismāʿīl al-Nahdī, from ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥārith, from Sālim ibn Abī Ḥafṣah al-ʿIjlī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

There were three qualities in the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله that were not in anyone other than him: he had no shadow; and he would not pass through a road, then someone would pass through it after two or three days, except that it would be recognized that he had passed through it due to the pleasantness of his fragrance; and he did not pass by a stone or a tree except that it prostrated to him.

key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, referring to the Prophet Muḥammad
key_terms.طَرِيقٍ: a road or pathway through which he passed
key_terms.طِيبِ عَرْفِهِ: the pleasantness of his fragrance by which his passing was recognized

ai.seo_question: What unique signs and miracles are reported about the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith describes three unique signs associated with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: the absence of a shadow, the lingering recognition of his fragrance, and the prostration of stones and trees before him. It presents these as distinctive marks of his exalted prophetic station and miraculous qualities.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad and someone else, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed Shabab Al Sayrafi, from Malik Bin Ismail Al Nahdy, from Abdul Salam Bin Haris, from Salim Bin Abu Hafsa Al Ijaly,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There were three (qualities) in Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> which did not happen to be in anyone apart from him<sup>saww</sup> – There did not happen to be a shadow for him<sup>saww</sup>, and it was so that he<sup>saww</sup> did not pass by a street; and no one would pass through it after two days or three, except that one would recognise that he<sup>saww</sup> had passed through it, due to the (still left therein) fragrance of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> (making him<sup>saww</sup>) recognised; and it was so that he<sup>saww</sup> neither passed by a rock nor by a tree except these prostrated to him<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Muhammad and others have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid Shabab al-Sayrafi from Malik ibn ’Isma‘il al-Nahdi from ‘abd al-Salamibn Harith from Salim ibn abu Hafsa al-‘Ijli from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“The Messenger of Allah had three qualities that no one else had. He did not have any shadow. Whatever path he would walk even after two or three days one could still notice his passing thereby due to his fragrance that remained along the path. Whatever stones and trees that he would pass by it would prostrate for him our of respect.”
